commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts need a follow-up date so agents know when to contact them
next. Add a FollowUp value class that accepts dates in DD-MM-YYYY
format only and rejects dates that do not exist, such as 31-02-2026.

The class is not wired into Person yet; that will be done separately.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align delete messages with the feature spec
commitResults.messageBody:
Show only the contact's name when a contact is deleted, and refer to
contacts instead of persons in the delete usage and invalid index
messages, as described in the MVP feature specification.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Easy-Insurance as the product name on site
commitResults.messageBody:
The navbar and page titles said EasyInsurance, while the README and
the guides say Easy-Insurance. Use Easy-Insurance everywhere.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace AB3 names users see with Easy-Insurance
commitResults.messageBody:
The window title, JAR file, log file and startup log lines still used
the AddressBook names. Rename them to Easy-Insurance so the app matches
the product name, and update the guides that mention the JAR name.

The data file keeps its name, so contacts already saved in
data/addressbook.json still load.

Agents need to record when to contact someone next. Contacts can now
have an optional follow-up date:
* add accepts an optional f/DD-MM-YYYY, and warns if the date is in the
  past (it is still saved, so agents can record past follow-ups).
* The follow-up date is saved to and loaded from the data file. Data
  files without it still load, as contacts with no follow-up.
* The contact card shows the follow-up date, or None.
* edit keeps the existing follow-up date when other details change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null entries in the data file instead of crashing
commitResults.messageBody:
A JSON null inside the persons list or a contact's tags list made the
app fail during start-up with a NullPointerException. Treat both as
invalid data so the existing recovery path starts with an empty list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix documentation inconsistencies found in the release check
commitResults.messageBody:
Use an add example that is not already in the sample data so it works
on a fresh install, name the follow-up parameter FOLLOW_UP_DATE
everywhere, point the setup guide at JDK 25 and Easy-Insurance, and
remove a duplicated responsibilities line on the About Us page.

commitResults.messageTitle: Back up unreadable data file before starting empty
commitResults.messageBody:
The app used to start empty and overwrite a bad data file on the next
save. It now copies the file to <name>.bak first so users can fix and
restore it.
Tests already run with assertions on, but manual runs did not.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bundle Apple Silicon JavaFX natives in the JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
The JAR only had x86_64 macOS natives, so it failed to start on Apple
Silicon Macs using a JDK without JavaFX.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow the displayed contact list to be sorted
commitResults.messageBody:
The due command needs to show follow-ups earliest first. Any plain
filter update resets the order, so other commands keep the stored order.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add due command for upcoming follow-ups
commitResults.messageBody:
Agents need to see who to call today and this week. Overdue dates are
also marked on the contact card.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the due command in the developer guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Tighten backup helper visibility and logging
commitResults.messageBody:
The backup suffix is only used inside the storage class, so it is now
private. A successful backup is logged at info level because the load
failure itself is already reported as a warning by MainApp.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy follow-up label and due parser constants
commitResults.messageBody:
The contact card built its follow-up label twice and used inline
strings, and the due parser kept its regex inline. Named constants
make the intent clear. Split a test that checked two methods so each
test name follows the method_scenario_expected convention.
